items.title: Perodua QV-E: A much better deal than it was at launch
items.summary: THE biggest improvement to Perodua QV-E since its Sepang debut a few months ago is not something you can see from behind the wheel. It is the way Perodua has changed the ownership proposition. In fact, spending more time with Perodua's first EV makes its original pricing look even more unfortunate.

items.title: MCMC denies involvement in activities described in Anthropic report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has denied involvement in activities or arrangements described in a recent report by artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic. In a statement, MCMC said it was aware of the report and took the matters raised seriously. "For clarity, activities of the nature described in the report do not form part of MCMC's functions or mandate, and MCMC does not engage in such activities or arrangements."

items.title: Widowed mother of four guts fish, collects boxes to feed children
items.summary: Nor Aza Hamzah, 44, said she frequently apologises to her youngest daughter for being unable to buy her a birthday cake due to financial hardship. She said her 6-year-old daughter, Aimy Mariam, often cries after seeing her friends celebrate birthdays at school or eateries. To support her children, Nor Aza takes on multiple odd jobs, including gutting catfish for RM3 a kg, collecting cardboard boxes along roadsides, and selling used cooking oil.

items.title: Duopharma Biotech confirms cyberattack on it infrastructure
items.summary: Preliminary investigations indicate that a set of data files had been exfiltrated, allegedly including personal data. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the pharmaceutical company said the incident was detected by its internal cyber defence systems, which identified an unauthorised system access attempt. Duopharma Biotech said that following the containment, the company initiated a comprehensive incident response review.

items.title: 30 Malaysians arrested in Indonesia over alleged online scam syndicate
items.summary: JAKARTA: Thirty Malaysians suspected of operating an online scam syndicate targeting their compatriots were arrested at a hotel in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, on Tuesday. Pontianak Immigration Office chief Sam Fernando said the group occupied 14 hotel rooms to carry out their operations, which aimed to defraud Malaysian citizens. Initial investigations indicate no Indonesian nationals were targeted.

items.title: KL DOE warns of fake procurement scams after two suppliers lose more than RM200,000
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — The Kuala Lumpur Department of Environment (DOE) has detected several attempts by irresponsible parties to commit fraud using the department’s name. She said her department first detected the scam on September 4, when a representative of a diving equipment supplier came to the department to verify the authenticity of government procurement documents. “Prior to that, KL DOE also received several inquiries regarding these government procurement documents starting in mid-August, and last Tuesday (September 8) from a supplier company representative who also came to inquire about a souvenir order worth more than RM100,000 supposedly made by KL DOE for an upcoming programme,” she told Bernama, here today.

items.title: Fire Dept: Two men found dead in separate incidents in Penang drain and Perak river
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 11 — Two men were found dead in separate incidents in Penang and Perak today, one in a drain near a school here and the other in Sungai Perak. The body of Ooi Chai Siang, 37, was found in a drain about 1.5 metres deep near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Tun Hussein Onn in Taman Kelisa Emas here today. Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received a call from the police at 12.10pm requesting assistance to retrieve the body.

items.title: German tourist dies after fall during Mount Jasar hike
items.summary: CAMERON HIGHLANDS: A 58-year-old German tourist died after falling while hiking up Mount Jasar with his wife today. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Zulfadli Zakaria said 16 personnel from the Cameron Highlands station were deployed after receiving an emergency call at 12.04pm. Rescue personnel, assisted by police, Civil Defence Force personnel, and Cameron Highlands Forestry Office officers, carried the body down a dangerous slope amid heavy rain, taking nearly three hours.

items.title: Petronas, Jogmec strengthen LNG collaboration via master agreement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas LNG Ltd (PLL) has entered into a Master Sales and Purchase Agreement (MSPA) with the Japan Organisation for Metals and Energy Security (JOGMEC) to safeguard Japan's energy security while respecting Malaysia's domestic supply needs. According to the statement, the MSPA reflects Petronas' ongoing commitment to delivering reliable energy solutions and fostering strategic partnerships that contribute to a secure, sustainable and resilient energy future. The framework reinforces Petronas' role as a reliable and trusted LNG supplier to Japan and underscores the shared commitment to ensure reliable energy supplies amid an evolving global energy landscape.

items.title: PM Anwar heads to India for BRICS summit, bilateral talks with world leaders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — After concluding his working visit to Sabah today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for New Delhi to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit, where he is also scheduled to hold several bilateral meetings. In a Facebook post, Anwar said he was scheduled to meet the Prime Minister of India, as well as the presidents of Russia, Iran and Kazakhstan and the Prime Minister of Ethiopia. “My delegation and I have departed for New Delhi, India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.

items.title: Rosmah touched by "Rindu saya ka?" Najib cutout at Umno general assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor said she was touched by an Umno supporter who brought a life-sized cutout of her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to the Umno general assembly today. In a Facebook post, Rosmah said the gesture by the supporter, known as "Mr J", reflected the longing among Najib's supporters for the former Umno president. "Datuk Seri Najib is on the way to PWTC," said Mr J to those missing the former prime minister.

items.title: Southern Score bags RM180mil Melaka hospital job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Southern Score Builders Bhd has secured a RM180 million contract to undertake the main building works for a private hospital development in Bukit Katil, Melaka. The contract covers constructing a seven-storey private hospital, a three-storey car park, a mechanical and electrical utility building, a pump house, a waste house and a VIE tank facility. The project is a related-party transaction because the siblings of Southern Score director and major shareholder Tan Sri Datuk Seri Gan Yu Chai are the director and major shareholder of Radium Development Bhd.

items.title: Finas to tighten filming permit rules to ensure content compliance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) will introduce additional conditions for filming permits to ensure productions comply with content guidelines and do not harm society. Finas said the move was among three agreements reached during a meeting with the Malaysian Islamic Development Department (Jakim) today to strengthen governance of film and television content. Finas said the initiatives reflected efforts to strengthen content governance while maintaining a balance between creative expression and societal sensitivities.

items.title: Past is past, but Umno delegates want PAS to prove it can be different
items.summary: At 68, the Umno Kuala Krai division secretary has seen the party’s relationship with PAS shift from cooperation to rivalry and back again. Muhammad said any renewed cooperation between Umno and PAS would require both sides to make compromises, particularly over the allocation of seats in the next election. PAS members attend the Umno Youth General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur yesterday.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPTEMBER 11, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower on Friday amid another round of selling across regional markets, as persistently high crude oil prices continued to weigh on market sentiment. The recent weakness was largely externally driven, with Malaysia's underlying fundamentals remaining intact. In the cryptocurrency market, Bitcoin fell to RM313,469.

items.title: George Kent partners AI firm to expand tech footprint in Asean
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: George Kent (Malaysia) Bhd is strengthening its technology footprint through a collaboration between its wholly-owned GK SuperTech Sdn Bhd and Shandong Extreme Vision Technology Co Ltd. The latter is a Hong Kong-listed artificial intelligence (AI) technology company. The collaboration gives GK SuperTech exclusive rights to rebrand, market, distribute and sell Extreme Vision's AI algorithms and large models in Malaysia and Singapore.

items.title: Single mother fined RM1,800 for assaulting man at Melaka Sentral
items.summary: MELAKA: A single mother of four was fined RM1,800 by the Ayer Keroh magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to assaulting a man at an eatery in Melaka Sentral in July. Magistrate Sharda Shienha Mohd Suleiman imposed the sentence on Nurul Amalina Mohamad Kamal, 32, after taking into account her guilty plea, mitigation, the facts of the case and the prosecution's submission on sentencing. Amalina was charged with voluntarily causing hurt to Mohd Zubir Maarof, 47, together with four other people who had previously been charged.

items.title: Don't let rivals' narratives divide Umno, veterans warn
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must not allow political pressure from its opponents to divide the party or turn its own members into conduits for narratives built by its rivals, said Veteran Umno. Reading out their resolutions at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, the group's committee member Datuk Adam Abd Hamid said the party must remain united in facing political pressure and attacks. "Umno must be the leader, not merely a complement, in shaping Malay political power," it said.

items.title: Serian still tops API reading nationwide with 'very unhealthy' 220
items.summary: Another 47 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings. In Sabah, moderate readings were recorded in Kimanis at 96, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (94), Kota Kinabalu (91), Keningau (63) and Sandakan (58). Labuan recorded a moderate reading of 97, while Kapit (95) and Limbang (80) in Sarawak also remained in the moderate category.

items.title: Citaglobal bags RM82.1mil residential college job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd has secured an RM82.1 million design-and-build subcontract for the new residential college at Institut Pendidikan Guru Bahasa Melayu here. Citaglobal said its subsidiary Citaglobal Land Sdn Bhd accepted a letter of award from Purnama Base Sdn Bhd for the project. Citaglobal said the project is part of a government development initiative in the education sector, implemented through the Public Works Department (JKR).

items.title: PTT Synergy buys Penang land for RM62.53mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PTT Synergy Group Bhd subsidiary PTT Logistics Hub 3 Sdn Bhd is buying a plot of freehold land in Seberang Perai Selatan, Penang for RM62.53 million. In its filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said PTT Logistics signed a sale and purchase agreement (SPA) with Lee Mooi Khean for the acquisition. "The proposed acquisition is a strategic investment undertaken in line with the company's long-term growth and expansion objectives.

items.title: Umno grassroots open to closer Pas ties if it benefits the people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno grassroots are unlikely to reject closer cooperation with Pas if it benefits the rakyat, said a Melaka Umno leader. Duyong assemblyman Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, who is also a deputy Melaka state executive councillor, said any potential cooperation between the two parties must be built around common ground without either side compromising its core principles. "Political cooperation is a political strategy.

items.title: IHH maintains claim on Fortis losses, respects court decision
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare maintains its claim that it suffered losses due to delays in obtaining the mandatory tender offer approvals required for its acquisition of Fortis Healthcare. IHH and its indirect wholly owned subsidiary Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd (NTK) were unrelated parties to that dispute. IHH said in a statement that the group and NTK respected the judgment issued by the Tokyo District Court on Sept 10.

items.title: Economy minister: Sabah receives RM582m, highest allocation for small-scale projects nationwide since 2023
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — A total of RM1.52 billion has been allocated for 8,069 small-scale projects and People’s Facility Initiatives (IKR) nationwide since 2023, with Sabah receiving the largest share at RM582.29 million for 2,301 projects. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said RM175.24 million of the allocation for Sabah was channelled for the implementation of 985 IKR projects, and RM407.05 million was for 1,316 small-scale projects. For this year alone, he said, Sabah received RM113.3 million to implement 481 IKR and small-scale projects, out of a total national allocation of RM323.8 million.

items.title: Five killed in Thursday's Dutch coach crash in Switzerland
items.summary: GENEVA: Five people were killed when a coach carrying Dutch tourists in eastern Switzerland crashed this week, police said on Friday. The accident happened on Thursday afternoon in the eastern canton of Graubunden. The coach hit a safety barrier before overturning and plunging down an embankment, a local police spokesman told Swiss media on Thursday.

items.title: GISBH fails in bid to challenge Kedah fatwa declaring teachings deviant
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — The Alor Setar High Court has dismissed an application by GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and its Chief Executive Officer, Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, for leave to initiate judicial review proceedings to challenge a state fatwa issued against them last year. The fatwa, issued by the Kedah State Fatwa Committee on February 12 last year, ruled that the beliefs, teachings, tenets and practices of GISBH members and followers were deviant and contrary to Islamic teachings. The applicants named the Kedah State Fatwa Committee, Kedah State Islamic Religious Council and Mufti of Kedah as respondents.

items.title: Malaysia's disaster expertise sought by global resilience coalition
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Malaysia should join the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) to share its expertise in managing natural disasters, says its director-general Amit Prothi. CDRI director-general Amit Prothi said Malaysia, as an Asean member, had extensive experience in dealing with disasters including landslides, tsunamis and major earthquakes. He said the coalition was keen to strengthen cooperation with Asean countries and regional organisations, including the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre) in Indonesia.

items.title: Hextar Industries RM177.48 mln woodpeckers deal falls through
items.summary: In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Hextar Industries said the conditional share purchase agreement (SPA) entered into between the company and the vendors on Feb 12, 2026, had lapsed today. "Accordingly, the proposed acquisition will not proceed," the company said. The company made announcements relating to the proposed acquisition on Feb 12, June 12 and June 23, 2026.

items.title: Penang LRT works to close part of Jalan Magazine for 21 days from Sept 14
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 11 — Jalan Magazine here will be closed for 21 days from September 14 to facilitate road widening and utility relocation works for the LRT Mutiara Line project. “The closure will involve the leftmost lane of Jalan Magazine in front of St. Giles Wembley Hotel heading towards KOMTAR, while the other lanes will remain open to traffic,” it said in a statement today. It said a partial lane closure would also be implemented intermittently along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah from 8am to 4pm daily from September 16 to December 15 to facilitate construction of the LRT Mutiara Line, including drainage and road widening works.

items.title: Umno Overseas Club proposes emergency network for Malaysians abroad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Umno Overseas Club has proposed setting up a community emergency response network to help Malaysian diplomatic missions assist citizens abroad during crises. Newcastle Umno Overseas Club president Muhammad Amir Ikram Mohd Fadil said the network could link Malaysian communities abroad with embassies and consulates to help identify citizens who needed urgent assistance. Amir said Malaysian communities abroad were often better placed to identify the immediate needs of fellow Malaysians during emergencies because they were already present in affected areas.

items.title: Vestland secures RM410mln contract for Jalan Ampang development
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd's wholly owned subsidiary Vestland Resources Sdn Bhd (VRSB) has secured a RM410 million contract from Golden Armani Sdn Bhd for construction works in Jalan Ampang, Kuala Lumpur. The development involves a 69-storey small office home office (SOHO) tower and a 78-storey small office versatile office (SOVO) tower. "The scope of works includes the design, approval, construction, completion, testing and commissioning of the related works.

items.title: Anwar departs for India to attend 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has departed for New Delhi, India, to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. During his visit, Anwar is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Among the leaders expected to attend are Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto.

items.title: Zoo Negara says all animals safe after flash floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Flash floods at Zoo Negara two days ago were triggered by persistent heavy rain that caused water from Sungai Pandan and Sungai Kemensah in Hulu Klang to converge and overflow. Zoo Negara deputy president Datuk Rosly Lana said none of the animals were injured or killed despite floodwaters reaching up to 1.2min several areas. Rosly said water from the two rivers quickly overflowed into several animal enclosures, affecting routes used by visitors and staff.

items.title: 'Exorcism' murder: Court acquits healer who suffered from schizophrenia
items.summary: The High Court acquitted 55-year-old Che Hong Chiew of murdering her client, 41-year-old Lim Sin Hue, after ruling that Che was of unsound mind during the violent episode. Lim agreed to undergo a week-long Buddhist healing ritual at Che's residence in Pandan Perdana, Ampang. Sometime around 5pm, Che told Lim's mother that the 41-year-old had died, and apologised.

items.title: Umno must secure written agreements to prevent betrayal in political cooperation, says delegate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must secure written agreements to safeguard its interests in future political cooperation and guard against another betrayal, said Perlis delegate Datuk Dr Fathul Bari Mat Jahya. Fathul Bari, who is Kangar Umno division chief, urged the leadership to prioritise the party's rights and political survival in negotiations, saying cooperation required sacrifice without compromising its dignity. Fathul said bargaining was part of political negotiations and Umno should not hesitate to assert its rights.

items.title: Malaysia needs extensive EV policy to spur localisation, not just higher taxes: Experts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia should take lessons from Thailand's higher tax policy on completely built-up (CBU) electric vehicles (EV) but industry experts caution that simply raising taxes will not be enough to drive meaningful localisation. Automotive analyst Shamsul Yunos said Thailand's use of tax pressure had helped push automakers towards local production, while Malaysia had traditionally taken a more measured approach. On Thursday, reports said that Thailand's EV board had approved plans to raise excise taxes on imported EVs in a bid to stimulate investment in its domestic automotive manufacturing sector.

items.title: [UPDATED] All southbound lanes reopened after North-South Expressway landslide
items.summary: IPOH: All southbound lanes on the North-South Expressway (Plus) at Km263.6 have been fully reopened following a landslide earlier today, according to the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM). However, traffic congestion stretched for 8km from the Menora Tunnel towards Ipoh Utara following the incident. LLM reported that congestion originally stretched for 4km before worsening to 8km by 5.15pm.

items.title: Malaysians scamming Malaysians: Indonesia nab 30 in Pontianak hotel raid
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 11 — Indonesian authorities have detained 30 Malaysians suspected of running online scam activities from a hotel in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, allegedly targeting fellow Malaysians. Pontianak Immigration Office chief Sam Fernando said the Malaysians, comprising 22 men and eight women, were detained along with a Taiwanese man at the hotel at about 11.15am on Tuesday in a joint operation with Pontianak City Police following intelligence on suspicious activities involving foreigners. Sam said the 31 foreign nationals had used 14 rooms in the hotel for their activities.

items.title: Chief minister says Melaka election not far off, dissolution of DUN required by year‑end
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 11 — As talks and speculation on the upcoming Melaka state election intensify, Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has hinted that the wait will be neither too long nor too soon. Speaking to the press during the 2026 Umno General Assembly at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL), Rauf said that that Melaka must dissolve its state legislative assembly (DUN) by the end of December as its five year term is nearing completion. “We can’t delay the dissolution of the DUN because the date is inching closer,” Rauf said.

items.title: DNA results for five Long Lellang crash victims due by tomorrow, say Sarawak police
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 11 — The deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) analysis for all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday is expected to be completed by tomorrow at the latest. “We anticipate that the DNA analysis for the five victims could be completed by tomorrow at the latest,” he told reporters here today. Last Tuesday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.

items.title: Newborn’s body found in Dungun hostel locker, police investigating
items.summary: DUNGUN, Sept 11 — A 19-year-old student allegedly hid her newborn baby’s body in a hostel locker after giving birth in a toilet at an educational institution here two days ago. Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the discovery of the body at 10.48pm yesterday. Investigations found that the student allegedly wrapped the baby in cloth, placed the body in a bag, and kept it in a hostel locker.

items.title: Tanker driver, still hospitalised, charged with murder over Pahang crash that wiped out young family on Merdeka Day
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Sept 11 — A cement tanker driver receiving treatment at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah was charged today with four counts of murder over a crash that killed four people on Aug 31. Zulkarnain is accused of having caused the deaths of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef Muhammad Nazatullah and Seow Beng Wai. He said Seow’s son, Sebastian Seow Jhen, 18, who was driving the Honda CR-V, and the tanker driver sustained serious injuries and were treated at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah in Temerloh.

items.title: Selangor sets Oct 26 as replacement holiday for Sultan’s Silver Jubilee
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 11 — Selangor has declared October 25 a special public holiday to commemorate the silver jubilee of Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah’s reign. State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the holiday would be replaced on October 26 as the anniversary falls on a Sunday, The Star reported. He added that the holiday would be observed in the same way as the September 1 public holiday marking Selangor’s overall victory at Sukma 2026.

items.title: Was bad weather to blame? Investigators dig into what brought down deadly Long Lellang chopper
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau has begun its investigation into the cause of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang which claimed five lives, said Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah. Hasbi said the ministry’s air accident investigation team was already at the crash site and was working to determine the cause of the tragedy. “We will wait for the report from the Air Accident Investigation Team.

items.title: PM Anwar visits Kampung Numbak fire victims, pledges aid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited and offered support to victims of the Kampung Numbak fire at the temporary relief centre at the Damai Multipurpose Hall here today. Anwar, accompanied by Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, arrived at the relief centre at 1.30 pm and spent about 20 minutes meeting the victims. The Prime Minister was then briefed on the fire by Kota Kinabalu Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah before handing over aid to the victims.

items.title: Zahid: Umno proposing ‘Grand Collaboration’ to end political clashes in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A proposal for the formation of a “Grand Collaboration” through political understanding (Tafahum Siyasi) among the country’s political party coalitions has been put forward to avoid political clashes that would be detrimental to the ummah and the nation, said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the concept does not involve a merger of political parties, but rather a common ground for mutual understanding aimed at preserving political stability and reinvigorating national economic growth. In other words, whoever Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) work with, Umno remains Umno, and Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional,” he said.

items.title: Anwar agrees Sarawak deserves fair share, promises formula clarity, interim measure by Malaysia Day
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim agreed to work towards establishing a formula for Sarawak to receive a share of the state’s revenue as he prepares to discuss an interim measure with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg. Anwar said Sarawak had put forward its views on a formula that would provide greater clarity on the matter, taking into account the federal government’s financial position and capacity. Anwar said he would continue discussions with Abang Johari over the next few days and hoped to announce an interim measure for Sarawak around the Malaysia Day celebrations in Kuching on September 16.

items.title: Sabah gets RM1.5b MA63 boost, Anwar hints Sarawak could be next by Sept 16
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The interim allocation for Sabah will immediately rise to RM1.5 billion this year, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said this in reply to a request from Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor during the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting (MTPMA63) press conference here. That is on behalf of the Sabah government,” said Hajiji.

items.title: From complaint to compensation: How victims in Malaysia are winning sexual harassment cases
items.summary: SEMPORNA, Sept 11 — The Sexual Harassment Tribunal Agency (Tags) under the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) recorded 134 sexual harassment complaints over a two-year period, with 90 of them successfully resolved. Male victims and children can also use this platform to seek redress. “Some victims have also won their cases and received compensation,” she told reporters after officiating the Semporna Zero Tolerance for Violence: Advocacy Against Sexual Harassment and End Violence Against Women programmes here yesterday.

items.title: DNA tests pending for five victims of Long Lellang helicopter crash, says Sarawak police
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 11 — The post-mortems on all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday were completed at 7.30pm yesterday. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the cause of death for all five victims was severe burn injuries sustained in the helicopter crash. On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.

items.title: Perak orders caterer at Lenggong boarding school to shut after almost 160 students, staff fall sick
items.summary: IPOH, September 11 — A food caterer serving a boarding school in Lenggong, Perak has been ordered to close after 159 students and staff developed symptoms of suspected food poisoning. Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the Hulu Perak District Health Office received a report of the incident from Lenggong Health Clinic on September 10. Sivanesan also urged food handlers to comply with the Food Act 1983 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 to prevent further food poisoning incidents.

items.title: No U-turn: Ex-minister Dr Zaliha says she has backed Health Service Commission proposal since 2023
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023. In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper. “In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper,” she said.

items.title: Anwar: Time to make MA63 part of the national conversation, not just Sabah-Sarawak issue
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to become part of the national narrative rather than being viewed solely as an issue concerning Sabah and Sarawak. He said the approach was important to ensure Malaysians understood that the government’s commitment to MA63 formed part of the Madani Government’s national policy and was closely linked to the country’s development, stability and unity. Anwar said this must be understood and embraced by people in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak as part of a national policy, commitment and narrative aimed at strengthening the country.

items.title: Sounds like a ‘PM in waiting’, Khairy says of Zahid’s speech at Umno assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s keynote at the party’s general assembly this morning earned praise from Khairy Jamaluddin. Khairy, an Umno returnee after being sacked three years ago for alleged disciplinary infractions and breaches of party discipline during GE15 – described the speech as crystal clear on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) direction ahead of the coming general election. “This is the speech of a prime minister in waiting and a speech of a government in waiting,” Khairy told reporters after Zahid’s speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly here.

items.title: Sabah, Sarawak to get bigger share of Parliament seats, Anwar says as MA63 push moves ahead
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Sabah and Sarawak will get a higher proportion of parliamentary representation under a Cabinet decision in principle to increase the number of seats for the two Borneo states, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. Anwar said the Cabinet had agreed to increase the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak, although the exact number and mechanism had yet to be determined. Anwar added that there could also be an increase in seats for peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: Zahid says Umno still hopes for favourable outcome after Najib clemency deferred
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today expressed disappointment over the postponement of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application, but said the party continues to hope for a favourable outcome. Zahid said Umno respected the decision and would continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers while appealing to His Majesty the King to use his wisdom in deciding Najib’s application. The Prime Minister’s Department today said Najib’s clemency application had been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.

items.title: State institutions won’t be political tools if BN returns to power, Zahid pledges at Umno assembly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today vowed that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools if Barisan Nasional (BN) returns to Putrajaya. Zahid said the pledge was part of BN’s proposed “Agenda Malaysia Biru”, a roadmap of eight initiatives aimed at shaping the country as it approaches its centenary of independence. Zahid said the initiative aimed to place Malaysia among the world’s top 20 countries in terms of integrity, governance and the rule of law.

items.title: ‘Time has come for BN to lead’: Zahid demands GE16 held as soon as possible
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today called for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible, saying the time had come for Barisan Nasional (BN) to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country. Zahid said GE16 would be a defining moment for Umno and BN to regain the mandate to lead, as he outlined the coalition’s “gelombang biru” (blue wave) strategy ahead of the next general election. Since we are already fighting, let us fight all the way,” he said.

items.title: Beyond data centres: What Budget 2027 needs to deliver, according to MBSB Investment Bank
items.summary: MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said there should also be focus on supply-side efficiency by broadening the tax base, closing leakages, expanding consumption excises, introducing carbon pricing, rationalising spending and crowding in private investment. “Budget 2027 should not only be assessed through fiscal expenditure. On the overall Budget 2027 allocation, MBSB IB said the budget is expected to remain moderately expansionary, with total federal government expenditure potentially reaching a new record of around RM440.9 billion, compared with Budget 2026’s RM421.2 billion.
